If we want to do the multivariate analysis, we can do like this. ::: {#43d8a3d6 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} sns.countplot(data = data, x = 'Survived', hue='Pclass') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-9-output-1.png){width=593 height=429} ::: ::: **Insights:** If we look at the above graph, we can see that most of the passengers who died were from the 3rd class. This is because the 3rd class had less access to lifeboats and safety measures compared to the 1st and 2nd classes. On the other hand, most of the passengers who survived were from the 1st class. This is because the 1st class had better access to lifeboats and safety measures compared to the 2nd and 3rd classes. ::: {#cd9e28d7 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} sns.countplot(data = data, x = 'Survived', hue='Sex') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-10-output-1.png){width=593 height=429} ::: ::: **Insights:** If we look at the above graph, we can see that most of the passengers who died were male. On the other hand, most of the survivors were female. ::: {#cf2c68bf .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} sns.displot(data=data, x='Age', kde = True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-11-output-1.png){width=470 height=470} ::: ::: **Insights:** There are some outliers in the age column. We can see that the graph is skewed to the right, which means that there are more younger passengers than older passengers. The majority of the passengers were between the ages of 20 and 40.
